headline: Mechanistic and latent models infer treatment response dynamics from sparse data
label: Mechanistic Treatment Response Modeling
summary: Sparse and indirect measurements constrain treatment response models that now encode time-dependent interactions and latent cellular states.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is inference of unobserved treatment response dynamics from limited or indirect data, using either explicit mechanistic structure or learned latent states. A physics-informed neural network learns time-varying cell interactions and treatment responses in a bladder cancer combination therapy model from sparse biological data. A Bellman-Harris branching process models chemotherapy-induced cell cycle dynamics, checkpoint adaptation and DNA repair. A probabilistic deep-learning model maps single-cell transcriptomes onto a latent dormancy pseudotime to locate cellular targets of anti-cancer therapies. What is new is explicit parameterization of time-dependent interactions and response mechanisms, fitted to sparse or indirect data to inform treatment strategy. The dormancy item relies on a learned latent state rather than an explicit mechanism, so the shared thread is dominant rather than universal.
